info.title: ChatRail API
info.description:
Send, schedule and receive WhatsApp messages through a linked-device session.

**Two things the API is careful about, which shape every endpoint below.**

*Accepted is not delivered.* A 202 means the message is durably stored and queued. Only the `status` field ever claims WhatsApp delivered anything, and `queued`, `submitted`, `sent`, `delivered` and `read` are deliberately distinct.

*A retry must not send twice.* Send `Idempotency-Key` on every send. A replay returns the original response; a concurrent duplicate is told to retry rather than allowed to race.

apiKey.description: A workspace API key, `cr_live_…`. Server-side only: it carries workspace authority and must never reach a browser.

post.description: Accepts a message for delivery and returns 202. **202 means accepted, never delivered** — the message is durably stored and queued, and only the `status` field ever claims delivery. Send `media` or `location` for an attachment, `send_at` to defer it. Supply `Idempotency-Key` so a retry cannot send twice.

400.description: The body, recipient or attachment was rejected.

402.description: The plan does not include this. The message names what would allow it.

409.description: The connection is not ready, or an identical Idempotency-Key is in flight.

422.description: The Idempotency-Key was reused with a different body.

get.description: Newest first, cursor paginated. Offsets are not offered: they skip and duplicate.

200.description: A page of messages and a `next_cursor`.
The message and its delivery timeline.

patch.description: Replaces the text of a text message this number sent, within WhatsApp's 15-minute window, and/or its `context`. Captions cannot be changed after sending. The first text is kept and audited. Editing the text does not change the context the AI answers from: send `context` too when the correction matters to it (a new gate, a new time). A context-only edit has no window and does not reach WhatsApp.

409.description: Not editable: received, not a text message, deleted, or past the window.

post.description: Only while it has not reached the provider. Once submitted the message exists on somebody's phone and cancelling would be a lie.

409.description: Already handed to the provider.

post.description: Sets this number's reaction on a message it sent or received; an empty `emoji` removes it. Works on any message that has reached WhatsApp.

409.description: Not possible for this message, or WhatsApp refused.

422.description: The connection's engine does not support reactions.

post.description: Shows blue ticks to the sender of an inbound message. Idempotent: a second call sends nothing.

409.description: Only a received message can be marked read.

patch.description: Currently `reject_calls`: decline incoming calls on this number automatically. Off by default, because the caller sees the call declined. Each call is still announced as `call.received`, with `rejected` saying whether it was declined.

delete.description: Soft deletes it and queues removal of its data.

post.description: Creates a WhatsApp group with this number as its owner. Everyone added counts against the member-add guardrail: at most 20 people per connection per hour, because adding people who did not ask to be added is how numbers get reported. Paid plans.

201.description: The new group, with its members.

429.description: Over the member-add guardrail for this hour.

get.description: Returns a bounded, name-sorted page for a group picker. Group ids use the same `from.group` representation delivered in message webhooks. Participant identities are never returned.

502.description: The transport returned an unreadable response.

get.description: Name, description, settings and members with their roles.

404.description: No such group for this number.

patch.description: Change the name or description, or who may send messages and edit group info. This number must be an admin of the group. Paid plans.

409.description: WhatsApp refused; not an admin?

post.description: `add`, `remove`, `promote` to admin or `demote`. Adding counts against the member-add guardrail (20 per connection per hour). Paid plans.

429.description: Over the member-add guardrail for this hour.

get.description: The chat.whatsapp.com link for joining the group.

post.description: Invalidates the current link and returns a new one.
This number leaves the group.
Shows "typing…" or "recording…" to a person or group, or stops (`paused`). WhatsApp clears it by itself after a short while or when a message arrives. Nothing is stored.

409.description: The connection is not ready.

422.description: The connection's engine cannot show typing.

post.description: Removes a message this number sent from every phone in the chat, within WhatsApp's window of about two and a half days. The record stays in ChatRail, marked deleted, and the deletion is audited.

409.description: Not deletable: received, already deleted, or past the window.
No longer scheduled.

get.description: Streamed row by row. **Message bodies are not included** — this is delivery metadata, not content.

get.summary: Check whether a number is on WhatsApp
get.description: Answers `checked: false` when the engine cannot say. Treat that as "send anyway": refusing a message because a check failed turns a missing provider feature into a delivery failure.

post.description: Returns `callback_token` **exactly once**. It cannot be retrieved again; store it when you receive it.

201.description: Created, with the one-time callback token.

402.description: The plan has no room for another number.

409.description: That slug is taken.

200.description: Every live connection in the workspace.

post.description: Issues a short-lived, single-use grant. By default it holds a QR; with `{"method": "code", "phone": "+447700900123"}` it holds a pairing code instead, which the person enters under Linked devices → Link with phone number (encoding `pairing-code`). Either is fetched once with the grant id: each is a pairing credential, so whoever uses it links *their* device to the number.

200.description: A grant id and its expiry.

409.description: The connection cannot be paired from its current state.

503.description: No transport is configured on this deployment.

get.description: Single use. A redeemed or expired grant is gone; ask for another.

409.description: Not in a suspendable state.
Not suspended.

post.description: Daily, weekly or monthly, resolved in the given IANA timezone. A schedule that fell behind fires once and drops the backlog rather than delivering days of stale messages.

400.description: Unknown timezone, or a recurrence that would never fire.

402.description: The plan does not include scheduling.

post.description: Keeps the schedule and stops it firing.

409.description: Not in a state that allows it.

post.description: The next run is computed from now. A schedule paused for a month does not fire the month it missed.

409.description: Not in a state that allows it.

post.description: Permanent. A cancelled schedule cannot be restarted.

409.description: Not in a state that allows it.

post.description: Returns the signing secret **exactly once**. Every delivery is signed with HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp, a period, and the raw request body; verify it and reject stale timestamps. The URL is validated at registration and the connection pinned at delivery, so an endpoint pointing at a private address is refused. Works with an API key holding `webhooks:write`, so a deploy script can register its own endpoint; every change is audited.

201.description: Created, with the one-time signing secret.

400.description: The URL is not publicly reachable over https.

402.description: Scoping to one connection is not on this plan.

post.description: Encrypted at rest and never returned. AI is off by default and enabled per connection.

402.description: AI is not on this plan.

get.description: Fingerprints and metadata only; the key itself is never returned.

put.summary: Set the AI policy for a connection
put.description: Draft or auto mode, with token, rate and monthly cost ceilings. Absent policy means AI is off for that connection.

example.system_instruction: Answer only from the attached context. If the answer is not there, say so.

402.description: AI is not on this plan.

get.summary: Get the AI policy for a connection
get.description: Absent policy means AI is off for that connection, which is the default.
Usage, cost, outcome and the proposed reply. The assembled prompt is represented by its hash and the list of context keys that went into it, never reproduced.

post.description: Accepts the pending draft through the normal durable message outbox.

409.description: The draft cannot be sent.

post.description: Removes a pending draft from the human review queue without sending it. Supply a reason where you know it: the counts are what make draft quality measurable, and `wrong_correlation` in particular is the only signal that a reply was matched to the wrong alert.

409.description: The draft cannot be dismissed.

get.description: Streams the file from the transport through ChatRail. Inbound only: an outbound attachment's URL is one the caller supplied and already has. The response carries the stored content type, never the transport's, and is always served as an attachment. Answers 404 when the message has no attachment, when the transport reported a file it does not serve, or when it no longer holds it.

404.description: No downloadable media on this message.

503.description: This deployment cannot retrieve media from the transport.

post.summary: Correct which message a reply answers
post.description: Re-points an inbound reply at the outbound message it actually answers, or unlinks it with `null`. The engine's original choice is preserved, so corrections measure the correlation rules rather than quietly overwriting them. The previously linked alert reopens for correlation; the newly linked one is marked answered.

200.description: The corrected link, and what it overruled.

400.description: The target is not an outbound message in the same conversation.

409.description: Only an inbound message has a correlation to correct.

get.summary: Summarise what happened to AI drafts
get.description: Counts only, never text: drafts sent unchanged, sent after editing, or dismissed and why; runs that ran with no business context at all; and correlation corrections grouped by the rule that originally fired. Accepts `days` (default 30).
Shows exactly what the presented credential can do. The first call to make.

200.description: The principal, its scopes and its workspace.

get.description: Includes the plan and what has been used against it.

200.description: The workspace, the caller role and the plan.

get.description: Counts only. A count of messages is not a message; no content is reachable here.

post.description: Returns the key **exactly once**. It is stored only as a hash and cannot be recovered. A key may never hold more than the person issuing it.

403.description: Your role cannot grant those scopes.

200.description: Key metadata and prefixes, never the keys.

post.description: Issues a replacement and revokes the old one.

200.description: Members, invitations, and the roles this caller may assign.

post.description: Emails a single-use link bound to that address. The token is never returned in the response. Nobody may invite to a role above their own.

402.description: Member management is not on this plan.

409.description: Already a member.

post.description: Requires a signed-in session whose address matches the invited one. Possessing the token is not enough — a forwarded invitation email must not be a way into a workspace.

example.token: the token from the invitation link

401.description: Sign in as the invited address first.

403.description: The invitation was sent to a different address.
You cannot assign or act on that role.

409.description: A workspace must keep an owner.
A workspace must keep an owner.

post.description: Always answers 202, whether or not the address has an account. It is not an existence check and must not be presented as one.

202.description: A code has been sent if that address has an account.

post.summary: Exchange a code for a session
post.description: Every failure returns the same error — no code, wrong code, expired, too many attempts. Distinguishing them would reintroduce an oracle.

get.description: Which of Google and GitHub are switched on for this deployment, so a sign-in page only offers buttons that will work.

200.description: An object of provider name to boolean.

get.summary: Start a Google or GitHub sign-in
get.description: A browser navigation, not an API call: redirects to the provider with a state value and a PKCE challenge held in a short-lived HttpOnly cookie. An optional same-origin `next` path is where the person lands afterwards.

get.summary: Finish a Google or GitHub sign-in
get.description: Where the provider sends the person back. Only an address the provider has verified is accepted; it lands in the same account an emailed code for that address would. Always redirects to the sign-in page — with a session cookie on success, or `auth_error` on failure.

post.description: Model Context Protocol over a stateless streamable HTTP transport. Read-only by default; mutating tools preview and apply only when called again with `confirm: true`. No tool returns message content.

402.description: MCP is not on this plan.

200.description: The tools this credential may call.

post.description: Called by the WhatsApp transport, not by you. Authenticated by the per-connection token returned once when the connection was created. Redeliveries are deduplicated.

get.description: Never checks dependencies. Point a restart policy here, not a traffic probe.
Checks dependencies. Point the load balancer here.
Not registered unless `METRICS_TOKEN` is configured. No label carries a workspace, connection, number or session name.
